instruction: Someone greets you formally in the daytime. Greet them back with the same full formula.
explain: Jó napot kívánok = 'I wish (you) a good day' — the standard formal daytime hello.

instruction: Someone hands you something and says 'here you are'. Thank them.
explain: Köszönöm = thank you. Köszönöm szépen = thank you very much. Tessék = here you are.

instruction: Someone thanks you. Reply 'you're welcome'.
explain: Kérem (or Szívesen) answers thanks: 'you're welcome'. Kérem is the more formal one.

instruction: Make the question polite: put Elnézést (excuse me) and a comma in front of it.
explain: Elnézést = excuse me / sorry (literally 'forgiveness'). It opens any request to a stranger.
gloss: Excuse me, where is the shop?

instruction: Someone says goodbye formally. Say goodbye back with the full formal word.
explain: Viszontlátásra = 'until we see each other again', the formal goodbye. (Viszlát is the casual short form.)

instruction: Say the same thing about 'you' (te, informal): swap the pronoun and change the 'to be' word to the te-form.
explain: 'to be': én vagyok (I am), te vagy (you are). The pronoun can be dropped. 'You are American.'

instruction: Say it about Péter instead. In the 3rd person [he/she/it] the 'is' word disappears before a noun.
explain: 3rd person + noun: NO 'is' word and no 'a'. Péter tanár = 'Péter is a teacher.'

instruction: Answer yes in a full sentence. Ön is formal 'you'; answer about yourself with vagyok [I am].
explain: Ön takes 3rd-person forms, so the question has no 'is' word. Answer with vagyok: 'Yes, I am American.'

instruction: Answer with the cued place word. When you say WHERE something is, the 'is' word (van) stays, right after the place word.
explain: van is kept for location: Itt van a bolt = 'The shop is here.' (Dropped only before nouns/adjectives.)

instruction: Say it about 'we' (mi): swap the pronoun and use the we-form of 'to be'.
explain: mi → vagyunk (we are). 'We are here.' The pronoun can be dropped.

instruction: Say it about 'you all' (ti, informal plural): swap the pronoun and use the ti-form of 'to be'.
explain: ti → vagytok (you all are). 'You are here.'

instruction: Say it about 'they' (ők): swap the pronoun and use the they-form of 'to be'.
explain: ő itt van (he/she is here) → ők itt vannak (they are here). 'They are here.'

instruction: Point to something far away instead: swap ez (this) for az (that).
explain: ez = this (near), az = that (far). egy = a/an. 'That is a house.'

instruction: Say the key is over there instead: swap itt (here) for ott (there).
explain: itt = here, ott = there. 'The key is there.'

instruction: Answer 'This is a …' with the cued thing. Pattern: Ez egy + noun.
explain: Mi ez? = What is this? Ez egy könyv = 'This is a book' — no 'is' word needed.

instruction: Answer 'That is …' with the cued name. Pattern: Az + name.
explain: Ki az? = Who is that? Az Péter = 'That is Péter.' (Ő Péter = He is Péter.)

instruction: Answer with the cued number. After a number the noun stays SINGULAR [no plural ending].
explain: Hány = how many (+ singular noun). három = 3. 'There are three children here.'

instruction: Answer with the cued number. 2 is kettő on its own but két before a noun.
explain: két + singular noun: két ház = two houses. Standing alone: kettő. 'There are two houses here.'

instruction: Give Péter's age with the cued number. Pattern: name + number + éves [years old]; no 'is' word.
explain: Hány éves = how old. húsz 20 + öt 5 = huszonöt 25. 'Péter is 25 years old.'

instruction: Change the age to the cued number. Tens + units are written as one word.
explain: hatvan 60 + két 2 = hatvankét (két, not kettő, before éves). 'Péter is 62 years old.'

instruction: Someone asks your age formally (Ön). Answer with the cued number + éves + vagyok [I am].
explain: harminc = 30. About yourself add vagyok: 'I am 30 years old.'

instruction: Ask who it is: replace the name with the question word ki (who) and put it first.
explain: ki = who (for people). Question word first, no 'is' word: Ki ez? = 'Who is this?'

instruction: Ask what it is: replace egy könyv with the question word mi (what) and put it first.
explain: mi = what (for things). Mi ez? = 'What is this?' — ki for people, mi for things.

instruction: Ask where it is: replace itt with hol (where) at the front; van comes right after the question word.
explain: hol = where. The question word sits right before the verb: Hol van a bolt? 'Where is the shop?'

instruction: Someone asks formally how you are. Answer 'I'm fine, thank you' using the cued word.
explain: Hogy van? = How are you? (formal, Ön). jól = well → Jól vagyok = 'I am fine.'

instruction: Ask when: replace holnap (tomorrow) with mikor (when) and put it right before the verb.
explain: mikor = when; jön = comes. The question word sits right before the verb. 'When is Péter coming?'

instruction: Say it about two people: the noun after them needs the plural ending -k with a linking vowel [helper vowel] before it.
explain: Plural = -k; after a consonant add a linking vowel: tanár → tanárok. és = and. 'Péter and Anna are teachers.'

instruction: Swap in the cued noun and make it plural to match ők (they).
explain: Front-vowel noun → linking vowel e: gyerek → gyerekek. 'They are children.'

instruction: Swap in the cued word and make it plural. Describing words [adjectives] also take -k.
explain: Adjectives also take -k in the plural: amerikai → amerikaiak (linking a). 'They are Americans.'

instruction: Swap in the cued noun as the thing seen. The object ending [accusative] is -t; after a consonant add a linking vowel.
explain: Object = -t. Vowel-final autó → autót; consonant-final ház needs a linking vowel: házat. 'I see a house.'

instruction: Swap in the cued noun as the object. Front-vowel nouns take the linking vowel e before -t.
explain: könyv is a front-vowel word → linking vowel e: könyvet. 'I see a book.'

instruction: Order the cued thing instead. Some rounded-vowel nouns (ö, ü) take the linking vowel ö before -t.
explain: kávé ends in a vowel → just -t; gyümölcs → gyümölcsöt (linking ö). Kérek = I'd like. 'I'd like a fruit.'
gloss: I'd like a (piece of) fruit, please.

instruction: Introduce your father instead: swap the family word and keep the 'my' ending -m [possessive].
explain: -m = my. The final a lengthens: apa → apám. 'This is my father.'

instruction: Introduce your grandmother instead: swap the family word and keep the 'my' ending -m.
explain: nagymama → nagymamám (a → á + m). testvérem = my sibling. 'This is my grandmother.'

instruction: Change the nationality word. 3rd person + describing word [adjective]: no 'is' word.
explain: magyar = Hungarian (lowercase, like amerikai). No 'is' in the 3rd person. 'My grandfather is Hungarian.'

instruction: Swap in the cued place. 'In' = -ban/-ben; use -ban for back-vowel words (a, á, o, ó, u, ú).
explain: -ban/-ben = in. lakás has back vowels → -ban. 'I am in the flat.'

instruction: Swap in the cued place. 'Into / to (inside)' = -ba/-be; back-vowel word → -ba.
explain: -ba/-be = into (movement). város: back → -ba. 'I'm going into town.'

instruction: Swap in the cued place. 'Out of / from (inside)' = -ból/-ből; front-vowel word → -ből.
explain: -ból/-ből = out of. étterem: front → -ből. 'I'm coming from the restaurant.'

instruction: Swap in the cued thing. 'On' has three forms: -on (back vowels), -en (front), -ön (front rounded: ö, ő, ü, ű).
cue: A kulcs az asztalon van. → (a könyv)
explain: -on/-en/-ön = on. könyv has a rounded front vowel → -ön: könyvön. 'The key is on the book.'
gloss: The key is on the book.

instruction: Swap in the cued country. 'To' with Hungary and most Hungarian towns = -ra/-re (literally 'onto'); other countries take -ba/-be.
explain: -ra/-re = onto/to. Magyarország: back → -ra. Other countries take -ba/-be (Németországba). 'I'm going to Hungary.'

instruction: Swap in the cued town. 'From' = -ról/-ről. Budapest is an exception: it takes FRONT endings.
explain: -ról/-ről = from (off). Budapest takes front endings despite its back vowels: Budapestről. 'I'm coming from Budapest.'

instruction: Swap in the cued person as the receiver. 'To (someone)' = -nak/-nek [dative].
explain: -nak/-nek = to (receiver). Anna: final a → á, back vowels → -nak: Annának. 'I give Anna a book.'
gloss: I give a book to Anna.

instruction: Swap in the cued person. segítek (I help) needs -nak/-nek on the person helped.
explain: segíteni takes the dative. testvérem: front → -nek: testvéremnek. 'I help my sibling.'

instruction: Swap in the cued vehicle. 'By / with' = -val/-vel; after a consonant the v copies that consonant.
explain: vonat + val → vonattal: the v becomes a second t. 'I go by train.'

instruction: Swap in the cued person. 'With (someone)' = -val/-vel; the v copies the final consonant.
explain: anyám + val → anyámmal: the v becomes a second m. 'I'm talking with my mother.'

instruction: Make it 'your' (te) house: change the owner ending [possessive] from -m (my) to -d (your).
explain: házam = my house, házad = your house (-d, same linking vowel a). 'This is your house.'

instruction: Make it his/her (ő) book: the 3rd-person owner ending is -a/-e, with no linking vowel.
explain: könyvem = my book → könyve = his/her book (front word → -e). 'This is his/her book.'

instruction: Make it 'your' (ti, plural you) house: the owner ending is -tok/-tek/-tök after a linking vowel.
explain: házunk = our house → házatok = your (pl.) house: ház + a + tok. 'This is your house.'

instruction: Make it his/her (ő) grandfather. The apa-words are irregular in the 3rd person: apja, nagyapja.
explain: nagyapám = my grandfather → nagyapja (irregular, like apja, anyja). 'This is his/her grandfather.'

instruction: Say it about 'you' (te). With an indefinite object [egy + noun] the verb takes the indefinite endings: én -k, te -sz.
explain: Indefinite object (egy kávét): én kérek, te kérsz. 'You'd like a coffee.'

instruction: Say it about 'you' (te). With a definite object [a/az + noun] the verb takes the definite endings: én -m, te -d.
explain: Definite object (a házat): én látom, te látod. 'You see the house.'

instruction: Change the object to 'a book' (egy könyv). The verb must switch to the indefinite ending.
explain: a könyvet (definite) → veszem; egy könyvet (indefinite) → veszek. 'I buy a book.'

instruction: Change the object to 'the book' (a könyv). The 3rd-person definite ending is -ja/-i; s + ja fuses to -ssa.
explain: Definite 3SG = -ja; olvas + ja → olvassa (s + j → ss). 'Péter is reading the book.'

instruction: Add the coverb [prefix-like particle] el- (away, off) to the front of the verb, written as one word.
explain: The coverb el- attaches to the verb in a neutral sentence: elmegyek. 'I'm going off to Budapest.'

instruction: Add the coverb el- (here: 'through, to the end') to the front of the verb, as one word.
explain: el- + olvasom = elolvasom, 'I'll read it through'. Coverb stays attached; this completed-action form usually points to the future.
gloss: I'll read the book through (to the end).
